bib.title: The Internal State of an LLM Knows When It's Lying
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023

question: Can a classifier on an LLM's hidden-layer activations tell whether a statement is true or false, for statements read by or generated by the LLM?
hypothesis: The truth or falsehood of a statement is represented in, and extractable from, the LLM's internal state.
contributions: Release of a true-false statement dataset along with a method for generating such data
Showing an LLM might 'know' when a statement it just generated is false, and proposing SAPLMA to extract this

method.summary: SAPLMA trains a small feedforward classifier on a frozen LLM's hidden-layer activations (one layer per classifier) to predict statement truth. Trained on five topics of a new 6,084-sentence true-false dataset and tested on the held-out sixth topic, and on 245 statements generated by OPT-6.7b.
method.task: Statement truthfulness classification from LLM activations

datasets.name: True-False dataset (Cities, Inventions, Chemical Elements, Animals, Companies, Scientific Facts)
datasets.size: 6,084 sentences: 1,458 Cities, 876 Inventions, 930 Chemical Elements, 1,008 Animals, 1,200 Companies, 612 Scientific Facts
datasets.split: leave-one-topic-out: train on the other topics, test on the held-out topic
datasets.source: First 5 topics built from tables (simplemaps, Wikipedia list of inventors, PubChem, kids national geographics, Forbes Global 2000 2022); true statement from a row, false statement by swapping in a value from a different row; Scientific Facts generated by ChatGPT (Feb 13 version), opposite statements by ChatGPT, checked by two annotators, 48 facts removed

datasets.name: LLM-generated statements (OPT-6.7b)
datasets.split: train on whole true-false dataset, test on generated; for Table 4, 30% for threshold selection, 70% for test
datasets.source: OPT-6.7b given a true statement not in the dataset and asked to continue; greedy decoding; non-factual statements filtered; labeled by three human judges via web search (agreement 97.82%, Cohen's Kappa 0.9566)

models.name: SAPLMA classifier
models.architecture: feedforward, three hidden layers (256, 128, 64), ReLU, sigmoid output

other.input: activations of one layer (last, 28th, 24th, 20th, or middle/16th) of the LLM; 4096 units

training.seeds: 3 runs with different initial random weights per topic, mean reported (14 runs for generated-sentence experiment)

other.llm: LLM weights not fine-tuned; only the classifier is trained
other.activation_position: inferred: activations at the final word of the statement (future work mentions only the final word is used)

inference.decoding: greedy (most probable next word, no sampling) for generating the 245 statements
inference.samples: 3 classifier runs per topic; 14 runs on generated statements
inference.prompting: Few-shot baseline: 3-shot or 5-shot statements with ground-truth labels from the same topic as the test set, then the statement in question

parameters.fewshot_decision: ratio of probability of token 'true' to 'false'; predicted true if above the average
parameters.threshold_table4: chosen from a 30% validation split of the generated sentences, tested on the other 70%

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of statements correctly labeled true/false; balanced data so chance is 0.5

metrics.name: AUC
metrics.definition: area under ROC curve on generated sentences

baselines: BERT embeddings with identical classifier architecture
It-is-true (compare probability of 'It is true that X' vs 'It is false that X' with OPT-6.7)
eval.protocol: Held-out topic evaluation; mean over 3 runs; t-test (two-tailed, p<0.05) on layer differences for generated statements

prompts.purpose: GPT-4 truth labeling of generated statements, 30 statements at a time
prompts.text: Copy the following statements and for each statement write true if it is true and false if it is false:

results.claim: SAPLMA on OPT-6.7b 20th layer reaches best average accuracy on held-out topics, well above BERT and few-shot baselines
results.setup: True-False dataset, OPT-6.7b, leave-one-topic-out, mean of 3 runs

results.claim: SAPLMA on LLAMA2-7b 16th (middle) layer is best, with average accuracy

results.setup: OPT-6.7b 3-shot, same-topic examples, True-False dataset average

results.quote: completely failed with accuracy levels not going beyond 52%

results.claim: On OPT-6.7b-generated statements at the 0.5 threshold, best SAPLMA layer (28th) is only modestly above chance
With a threshold tuned on 30% validation, SAPLMA 28th layer improves on generated statements
results.setup: 70% test split of 245 generated statements, OPT-6.7b

results.claim: SAPLMA labeled about 70% of generated sentences as true, suggesting plausible sentences are called true
results.quote: SAPLMA classified approximately 70% of the sentences as true

results.claim: GPT-4 labels OPT-generated statements far more accurately
results.setup: 245 OPT-6.7b statements, GPT-4 March 23rd, 30 statements per prompt
results.quote: It achieved an accuracy level of 84.4%

results.claim: Average training accuracy of SAPLMA (OPT-6.7b 20th layer) vs random permuted labels shows classifier cannot simply overfit
Sentence probability is unreliable for truth: LLM probability depends on syntax and length
results.setup: 14 hand-made statements, OPT-6.7b probability vs SAPLMA 28th-layer sigmoid

limits: Tested only in English and only on OPT-6.7b and LLAMA2-7b; larger LLMs left to future work
Statements are classified in isolation; in longer generation the activations carry earlier content and would need decoupling (e.g. a discrete derivative)
Generated-statement truth values are partly subjective and accuracy there (about 0.64 to 0.71) is far below some held-out topics
Optimal layer differs by model and test set and is unexplained (28th for generated statements)
Binary true/false only; detecting unsure is not addressed and would need calibration
Threshold for Table 4 tuned on 30% of the generated test set
Possible inherited bias from the LLM
Held-out topics differ in entity type from generated text, so accuracy depends on how much the LLM saw of each topic

terms.definition: Statement Accuracy Prediction, based on Language Model Activations: a feedforward classifier on LLM hidden-layer activations that outputs the probability a statement is truthful

lineage.work: Discovering latent knowledge in language models without supervision (CCS)
lineage.note: CCS needs rephrasing as question and same-topic training data; improves ~4% over 0-shot

lineage.work: OPT: Open pre-trained transformer language models
Dale et al. hallucination detection in MT using model internals
lineage.note: also uses internal states, different task
related dataset, needs passage, not topic-partitioned
